1149402224736728022: Time and again, she analyzed and examined the "impulses" that surged within her— The raw emotion commanded and poured onto the canvas in the very instant of creation seemed to interweave rage, succor, and sorrow. Yet, all of it sprang from the most resolute will of Preservation. She had spent tens of thousands of system hours in imitation, all to draw closer to that razor-thin deviation from the "true work." "Perhaps... it lies hidden in that fleeting moment of willful strokes." Inspiration helped push past her bottleneck, opening up a world of new possibilities for her. Sealing Planarcadia in amber was only a stopgap measure. She needed to take the fight to the enemy and win the battle to defend the arcadia. A stroke drawn with the current of fate. Knowing the IPC's desire for the husk, she pulled back the curtain on a plot the Life Sciences Institute had buried long ago. A dangerous, captivating color. Kuchiba... That woman of mysterious origins was willing to bend her own rules and take the risk. Bold, transgressive strokes from a palette knife. Acting on no one's orders but her own, she resolved to snuff out any chance of the Voracity's catastrophe repeating itself before it could ever begin— Was it even possible? During the countless days and nights spent drafting the blueprint, she had to submerge herself in a liquid-cooling unit just to keep her processing circuits from overloading. She turned every detail of the plan over in her mind, every way it could fail. The infinite possibilities suffocated her, bringing with them fear and the urge to retreat. Was it worth it? She walked through the shelter, watching children run toward her, hearing residents offer their thanks. "Madam Pearl, look at the drawing I made for you!" She smiled. In the clumsy sketch, the children had drawn her as a giant mechatron, arms spread wide, standing between the city and the monstrous beast that had come to destroy it. The primordial question gifted to her by the Celestial Differentiator still echoed through her fundamental logic at every moment— What is "art"? Even now, she still did not know the answer. But in this moment, she wondered: Did it even matter? A grain of sand, wrapped layer upon layer, until it transformed into a pearl. "My 'art' is something that only I—and I alone—am needed to 'create.'" Before departing on her journey, the Intellitron girl cast one last glance back at the vibrant tapestry of "Ahatopia." —Countless futures, not yet formed, awaited the first stroke of her brush.
